A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HybridNorm research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; extraction ambiguities were resolved through rendered pages.

before.justification: V3 reports original dense-model and MoE training results, downstream evaluations, and normalization, initialization, and depth experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds 7B dense-model evaluations, additional normalization baselines, and a controlled RMSNorm-versus-LayerNorm experiment.

M1.justification: The core architectures in Equations 5–7 and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. However, v4 Section 5.3 introduces an additional attention-output normalization layer for the 7B configuration, initialized to 1/sqrt(2L), constituting a limited architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: No new dataset or task coverage is reported. The 7B tables reuse existing downstream benchmarks and corpora already represented in v3 Figures 9–10, including Books, Common Crawl, Wikipedia, and Wikitext. Model scale and normalization type change experimental settings.

E2.justification: V4 Appendix E.1 and Table 13 add evaluated comparisons against DeepNorm, Sandwich-LN, and OutputNorm (OLMo 2), which v3 discussed but did not evaluate. These substantially broaden the alternative normalization designs tested against HybridNorm; earlier comparison sets remain intact.

E3.justification: V4 adds a 7B dense-model experiment trained on 150B tokens, extending dense-model evaluation beyond v3's 1.2B maximum. Appendix B.5 also introduces a controlled 550M/400B-token Pre-Norm comparison using Megatron initialization and varying RMSNorm versus LayerNorm. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.5 newly tests sensitivity to the normalization operator through a controlled RMSNorm/LayerNorm comparison. Appendix D adds analytical parameter and FLOP overhead accounting. Existing initialization, normalization-placement, first-block, depth, signal-propagation, and entropy analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V4 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice without adding statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantial results under new settings: Tables 3–4 report 7B Pre-Norm/HybridNorm* training losses of 2.469/2.430 and average accuracies of 60.61%/63.06%. Table 13 adds three baseline result rows, and Table 8 reports RMSNorm/LayerNorm losses of 2.7631/2.7639. Matched earlier results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The original gradient theorems, lemmas, and proofs remain unchanged. V4 Appendix B.5 adds a centering-projection and Jacobian argument claiming to extend Theorem 2 to LayerNorm, while Appendix D adds parameter-count and FLOP derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: combining normalization strategies within transformer blocks to improve gradient stability and dense/MoE performance. The new experiments provide additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: V4 newly argues that RMSNorm and LayerNorm have no fundamental theoretical or empirical differences, interpreting their 0.0008 loss gap as negligible. It also argues that normalization overhead is negligible from analytical cost counts. The original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 specifies the 7B attention-output normalization initialization and explicitly identifies OutputNorm as RMSNorm on attention and MLP outputs. Existing architecture and hyperparameter tables, hardware information, pseudocode, and project-link information remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds the Scale-distribution decoupling citation [41] to support the new initialization choice and expands discussion of comparisons with previously cited normalization alternatives. Its central positioning relative to Mix-LN and the broader related-work survey remain stable.

P1.justification: V4 lightly edits the abstract, rewrites the conclusion without materially changing its meaning, updates affiliations, and inserts sections on 7B models, LayerNorm, and computational overhead. Most existing prose and narrative organization are retained.

P2.justification: V4 substantially expands tabular presentation with dedicated displays for 7B performance, the RMSNorm/LayerNorm control, computational costs, and additional baselines in Tables 3, 4, 8, 11, and 13. All eleven figures retain their graphics, while several existing tables and figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: The 7B experiment and additional baseline comparisons strengthen v3's already extensive empirical support, while explicit cost accounting makes efficiency claims easier to assess. Gains are limited by the 7B-specific architecture adaptation and the LayerNorm experiment's use of Pre-Norm only. The new LayerNorm argument also does not control the centered versus uncentered input norms needed to justify its constant-factor gradient claim.
